A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FaCT and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–M. The shorter v2 consolidates the bibliographies; it does not omit the scientific appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet and CUB experiments, concept-deletion evaluations, and a 38-participant interpretability study, with additional empirical analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical studies and reports revised concept-deletion curves in Figures 7, F1, and F2.

M1.justification: The B-cos architecture, bias-free TopK sparse autoencoder bottlenecks, and procedures for tracing concept contributions and input attributions are unchanged in Section 3 and Appendix A.

E1.justification: Both versions retain ImageNet classification, CUB-200 fine-grained classification, PartImageNet annotation comparisons, and the same user study. No dataset, task, population, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The comparisons retain CRAFT, CRP, and B-cos channels for concept consistency, and Saliency, Random, and Sobol for concept deletion. The revised deletion curves do not document any change to comparator membership or method definitions.

E3.justification: Appendix F still specifies 50 ImageNet classes, eight images per class, four Sobol designs, and the same deletion metrics and layers. Training, checkpoint selection, and user-study protocols also remain unchanged. No protocol revision is reported alongside the changed curves.

E4.justification: Figure F2 revises the empirical comparison for the existing control that preserves always-on concepts, particularly making Sobol more competitive. The control question remains unchanged, as do the other sparsity, consistency, stability, and misclassification analyses.

E5.justification: The three-seed random-baseline estimates in Appendix C.3, three-run runtime averages in Appendix I, and user-score distributions are retained. The revised deletion plots introduce no additional uncertainty estimates or significance tests.

E6.justification: Figures 7, F1, and F2 substantially revise baseline deletion curves under unchanged reported settings. In Figure 7's early DenseNet logit panel, at 100 deleted concepts, Sobol changes from approximately 0.78 to 0.02, while Saliency changes from approximately 0.20 to 0.91. This materially changes baseline rankings and FaCT's margins, although FaCT retains the strongest deletion performance.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation in Sections 3–4, C2-score definition, concept-entropy equations in Appendix D, and attribution and cross-layer derivations in Appendix H are unchanged.

C1.justification: Both versions claim faithful shared concept traces, improved concept consistency and interpretability, competitive ImageNet performance, and a new consistency metric. The abstract and introduction edits preserve these claims and their scope.

C2.justification: The interpretation of sharp deletion drops through always-on mean features is retained in Section 6 and Appendix F. Appendix L retains the same limitations concerning uninterpretable concepts, SAE dependence, and DINOv2-based evaluation.

D1.justification: Training details and Table A1, metric implementation details in Appendix C.3, deletion implementation details in Appendix F, and code/checkpoint access information are unchanged. The added architecture labels repeat identities already specified in Appendix F.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Deng et al.'s ImageNet database paper and Makhzani and Frey's K-Sparse Autoencoders. It also removes Discover-then-Name from the introduction's examples requiring predefined concept sets. Most bibliography changes consolidate existing appendix references or update metadata rather than expand research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 makes limited wording and grammar edits, adjusts the opening footnote, adds a funding acknowledgment, and unifies the main and appendix bibliographies. The scientific narrative and section organization remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 7 and F1 gain explicit DenseNet and ResNet labels, and Figure F2 reverses the architecture-panel order. There are limited text-flow and bibliography-layout changes. The figure and table inventory is retained; the substantial curve-value revisions are assessed under E6.

improvement.justification: The labeling, citation, and wording refinements improve clarity. However, the substantial baseline-curve revisions in Figures 7, F1, and F2 are unexplained despite unchanged reported settings, and sharply narrow the advantage over Sobol. The PDFs do not establish whether these revisions improve evidential reliability, preventing a confident judgment about the net change in paper quality.
